summary: Checks whether a value is **not** an array.
description: `nonArray(value)` is the same test as `!isArray(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
`Array.isArray` is the whole test, so an array from another frame counts and an array-like object — `arguments`, a `NodeList`, `{ length: 0 }` — does not.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not an array; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonArray("abc"); // => true
nonArray({ length: 0 }); // => true
nonArray(null); // => true
nonArray([]); // => false
nonArray([1, 2, 3]); // => false
```
